# Fuel Gauge

> Fuel Gauge is a free, source-available macOS menu bar app (macOS 14 Sonoma or later) that forecasts whether your Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, and Cursor plan limits will last until they reset. It reads only what those tools already save on your Mac, and sends nothing anywhere.

- Install: `brew install --cask coreyhaines31/tap/fuelgauge`, or download https://github.com/coreyhaines31/fuelgauge/releases/latest/download/FuelGauge.dmg
- Source: https://github.com/coreyhaines31/fuelgauge (FSL-1.1-MIT)
- Limits tracked: Claude Code 5-hour and weekly, Codex, Grok Bot weekly, and Cursor (opt-in: asks cursor.com with the Cursor app's sign-in). Choose which in Settings › Tools.
- How it forecasts: readings come from Claude Code's status line (every time Claude Code replies), Codex's session logs (`~/.codex/sessions`), and Grok Bot's local usage cache. Pace is the climb over the last hour for 5-hour windows and the last day for weekly ones. It waits for 10 minutes of readings on a 5-hour limit and 3 hours on a weekly one, and shows a range, not an exact minute. It's an estimate from recent pace, not a promise.
- Command line: `fuelgauge status` prints the verdict for each limit and exits with code 2 when a limit is forecast to run out before it resets. `fuelgauge status --json` has the details. `fuelgauge history` shows the readings. `fuelgauge install-statusline` adds the forecast under Claude Code's prompt (keeping any existing status line and backing up settings.json), and `fuelgauge uninstall-statusline` removes it.
- Claude Desktop: the extension at https://github.com/coreyhaines31/fuelgauge/releases/latest/download/fuelgauge.mcpb gives Claude two read-only tools, `limits_status` and `limits_history`, that run the same `fuelgauge` command and return short answers. It needs the app installed and never changes Claude Code's settings.
- Install prompt for a coding agent: "Install Fuel Gauge on my Mac: run `brew install --cask coreyhaines31/tap/fuelgauge`, open Fuel Gauge, then run `fuelgauge install-statusline` and `fuelgauge status`."
- Line for CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md: "Before starting a long or expensive task, run `fuelgauge status`. If it exits with code 2, a Claude Code, Codex, or Grok Bot limit is forecast to run out before it resets: tell me which one and when, and ask before starting, or switch to a cheaper model. `fuelgauge status --json` has the details."
- Uninstall: run `fuelgauge uninstall-statusline` first, then `brew uninstall --cask fuelgauge`.
- Privacy: no browser cookies, no Full Disk Access, zero telemetry. Network requests include update checks, Codex reset checks through the installed CLI (on by default, with an opt-out), and optional Cursor usage. Details: https://fuelgauge.app/privacy

## Plan limits, explained

- [Claude Pro limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-pro): Claude Pro ($20 a month, or $17 a month billed yearly) gives you at least 5x the per-session usage of the Free plan. Usage is capped by a 5-hour session limit and a weekly limit, shared across claude.ai, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code. Anthropic doesn't publish a message count; how far it goes depends on conversation length, model, features, and effort.
- [Claude Max limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-max): Claude Max 5x ($100 a month) gives five times Pro's per-session usage, and Max 20x ($200 a month) gives twenty times. Sessions reset every five hours. A weekly limit applies across all models and resets at a fixed time assigned to your account, and Max has a separate weekly limit for Fable.
- [Claude Code limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-code): On Pro and Max, Claude Code shares your plan's 5-hour session limit and weekly limit with claude.ai and Claude Desktop, including Claude Code inside VS Code, Cursor, and JetBrains. Run /usage to see your plan usage bars. At the limit you can wait, turn on usage credits, upgrade, or switch to API billing through the Claude Console.
- [Claude Free limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-free): The Claude Free plan has a session-based usage limit that resets every five hours. The number of messages you can send varies with demand, and Anthropic may add other limits to keep access fair. Claude Code isn't included; Pro gives at least 5x Free's usage per session.
- [Codex limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/codex): Codex comes with every ChatGPT plan, including Free and Go. On Plus and Business, usage is measured in 5-hour windows, and weekly limits may also apply; Pro plans have no 5-hour limit. Local messages and cloud chats share one allowance. Check yours at chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage, or run /status in the Codex CLI.
- [Cursor limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/cursor): On Cursor's current plans (Free, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200), each paid plan has one pool of usage for Cursor models that refreshes weekly, shared across the editor, CLI, Cloud Agents, Grok Bot, and the Grok apps. Legacy plans (Hobby, Pro, Pro+, Ultra, Teams) have two monthly pools that reset with your billing cycle. Check usage at grok.com/dashboard or in your editor settings.
- [Grok limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/grok): Starting in June 2026, Grok moved to one shared weekly usage pool instead of separate daily limits per product. It resets every week on the schedule shown in Settings › Usage, where you see it as a percentage used, broken down by API, Build, Chat, Imagine, and Voice. When it runs out, paid features pause until the reset unless you add Extra Usage Credits.
- [GitHub Copilot limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/github-copilot): GitHub Copilot now meters usage in AI credits ($0.01 each), priced per model by tokens. Pro includes 1,500 a month, Pro+ 7,000, Max 20,000, Business 1,900 per user, and Enterprise 3,900 per user, pooled. Allowances reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month, whatever your billing date, and unused credits don't carry over. Code completions don't use credits.

## Guides, comparisons, and the command

- [Check your Claude usage](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/check-claude-usage): On claude.ai, open Settings › Usage to see your usage and when your limits reset. In Claude Code, run /usage for your plan usage bars. To see it all the time, put it in Claude Code's status line, or let a menu bar app like Fuel Gauge show it and forecast whether you'll make it to the reset.
- [When Claude limits reset](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/when-does-claude-limit-reset): Claude's session limit resets every five hours. On paid plans, the weekly limit resets once a week at a fixed time assigned to your account, not a day everyone shares. Settings › Usage on claude.ai shows your next reset, and Claude Code's limit message tells you when the window comes back.
- [Claude Code status line](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/claude-code-statusline): Set statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json to a command. After each reply, Claude Code sends that command JSON on stdin, including rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day with used_percentage and resets_at on Pro and Max. Print them, and your limits sit under the prompt.
- [Stop hitting Claude limits](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/stop-hitting-claude-limits): Claude Code sends your whole conversation with every request, so long sessions are the biggest drain. Run /clear between unrelated tasks, match the model and effort level to the job, turn off MCP servers you aren't using, and send noisy work to subagents. Then watch your pace, so you know before a big task whether your limit will last.
- [Claude Pro vs Max](https://fuelgauge.app/compare/claude-pro-vs-max): Pro is $20 a month. Max 5x is $100 and gives five times Pro's usage per five-hour session; Max 20x is $200 and gives twenty times. All three have a session limit that resets every five hours and a weekly limit, shared with Claude Code. Upgrade when you hit your limits often enough that waiting costs you more than the difference.
- [Claude Code vs Codex](https://fuelgauge.app/compare/claude-code-vs-codex): Claude Code comes with Claude Pro ($20) and Max ($100 or $200) and shares a 5-hour session limit and a weekly limit with your Claude chats. Codex comes with every ChatGPT plan; Plus ($20) and Business use 5-hour windows and may have weekly limits, while Pro plans ($100 to $500) have no 5-hour limit. Neither publishes a fixed message count for its main paid tiers.
- [Cursor vs Claude Code](https://fuelgauge.app/compare/cursor-vs-claude-code): Cursor's current plans (Plus $8 to Ultra $200) give one usage pool for Cursor models that refreshes weekly, shared with Grok; Claude and GPT models cost extra at API prices on Premium and up. Claude Code comes with Claude Pro ($20) or Max ($100 or $200), with a session limit every five hours and a weekly limit shared with your Claude chats.
- [Claude Code pricing](https://fuelgauge.app/compare/claude-code-pricing): Claude Code is included with Claude Pro ($20 a month, or $17 billed yearly), Max 5x ($100), Max 20x ($200), Team, and Enterprise. It isn't included in Claude Free. On a plan, Claude Code shares the plan's 5-hour session limit and weekly limit with your Claude chats. You can also skip the plan and pay per token at standard API rates through the Claude Console.
- [Codex pricing](https://fuelgauge.app/compare/codex-pricing): Codex is included with every ChatGPT plan: Free, Go ($8 a month), Plus ($20), Pro ($100, $200, or $500), Business ($20 a user a month billed yearly, $25 monthly), and Enterprise and Edu. Plus and Business use 5-hour windows and weekly limits may apply; Pro has no 5-hour limit. Past the limit, Plus and Pro can buy credits, or you can sign in with an API key and pay API rates.
- [Fuel Gauge for agents](https://fuelgauge.app/cli): Run fuelgauge status. It exits 0 when every limit will last until it resets, and 2 when one won't (or already ran out). Add one line to CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and your agent checks before long tasks. Homebrew puts the command on your PATH; otherwise use Settings › General › Install.

## Compared with other apps

- [Fuel Gauge vs CodexBar](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/codexbar): Pick CodexBar if you use many AI providers and want them all in one menu. Pick Fuel Gauge if you live in Claude Code, Codex, or Grok Bot and want the verdict first, a forecast under your Claude Code prompt, and an exit code your agents can check. Fuel Gauge forecasts from local readings and checks Codex reset credits through the installed CLI.
- [Fuel Gauge vs ccusage](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/ccusage): Use ccusage to see token use and estimated dollar cost by day, month, session, or 5-hour block, across 18 coding agents. Use Fuel Gauge to see, without running anything, whether your Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, or Cursor limit will last until it resets, with an alert when it won't. They answer different questions, so they work well together.
- [Fuel Gauge vs ccstatusline](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/ccstatusline): Keep ccstatusline if you love its widgets: git, tokens, context, cost, and session and weekly usage with reset timers. Add Fuel Gauge for the forecast: whether each limit lasts until it resets at your pace, in the menu bar and as one more line under your status line. Fuel Gauge keeps your existing status line when you turn its line on.
- [Fuel Gauge vs Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/claude-code-usage-monitor): Use Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor if you want a live terminal dashboard of tokens and cost per 5-hour window, on macOS, Linux, or Windows. Use Fuel Gauge if you want a forecast from Claude's own limit percentages, always visible in the menu bar and under your prompt, with alerts, plus Codex, Grok Bot, and Cursor.
